Two directions for the holiday site

A style tile is the look before the layout. It shows the typefaces, the colors, the buttons and the way photography gets treated, so the conversation stays on how the site should feel rather than where the phone number goes. Pick a direction and every page gets built from it.

Prepared 4 September 2026 Brand Pam Hassler Interiors Scope Holiday decorating · Palm Beach & Martin County

The parent mark

Used everywhere. This is the business.

The seasonal mark

Holiday pages only, with the parent mark credited inside it. Keeping the site under Pam Hassler Interiors is deliberate: a holiday‑only identity would cost her work the other eleven months of the year.

What the brand already tells us

Typeface
Helvetica Light and Helvetica, set with wide letter‑spacing. Pulled from the business card artwork, so this is fact rather than guess.
Neutrals
Three warm greys, not blacks. Each carries a slight red bias, which is why the mark reads soft rather than corporate.

From the Santa’s Design Helpers artwork. It sits under the parent brand as a seasonal mark, so the two directions below differ mainly in how much work that red is asked to do.
Direction A

Quiet Evergreen

The design firm that happens to do Christmas. Warm paper, wide-tracked capitals lifted straight from her wordmark, and a deep pine that carries the season without saying holiday out loud. Red appears once per page, at most.

Best if she wants the holiday work to read as an extension of thirty years of interior design, and expects clients to hire her the way they’d hire an architect.

Christmas, handled

Design, installation and takedown for homes across South Florida. You come home to it finished.

Direction B

Candlelight

Evening, not morning. A dark warm ground makes the photography glow the way a decorated room actually looks at night, with brass and the campaign red doing real work instead of hiding. A softer serif carries the headlines.

Best if she wants the site to feel like the season itself, and to be unmistakably a holiday specialist the moment the page loads.

How to read this

  1. React to the feeling, not the words. The headlines are placeholders. If a direction feels right but a line is wrong, that’s a five-minute fix later.
  2. Pick one, or take pieces from both. A’s restraint with B’s dark gallery pages is a perfectly good third answer.
  3. The photography is real, and unretouched. Every image here is Pam’s own work, straight from the phone. Direction B leans dark partly because it flatters photos shot in low light, which most of hers are.

Both directions use the existing PH mark unchanged and free typefaces, so there’s no licensing cost either way. Contact details and service area are confirmed: Palm Beach County and Martin County. The headshot for the About page is still to come.
